content.title: Jimmy Butler on rejoining Warriors, start of ACL rehab: ‘I’m trying to get back out there’
content.text: WASHINGTON — Jimmy Butler couldn’t keep the smile off his face as he re-entered the Golden State Warriors’ universe for the first time since having surgery to repair his right ACL on Feb. 9. He hugged his teammates and coaches after reconnecting with the group before Monday’s game against the Washington Wizards.He also spoke to reporters for the first time since injuring the knee in a win over the Miami Heat on Jan. 19. Butler is confident he will play again sometime next season, but isn’t ready to give a timeline on his return yet as the rehab process gets started.“I feel like I just had surgery on my ACL five weeks ago,” Butler said as the smile crept across his face. “But all in all, I’m good, man. Happy.”Butler, who was acquired from the Heat just before the 2025 NBA trade deadline, said it has been “tough,” being away from the Warriors since being injured. The 36-year-old, six-time All-Star seemed to fit in well with the Warriors’ culture since the deal. He is trying to stay positive as the long rehab journey begins, but he acknowledged it’s been difficult being mostly away from the team for the last two months. Butler’s knee is still swollen, and he wasn’t cleared to fly again until recently.“Not being around my guys,” Butler said. “Hard. Not being able to play the game that I love. Not being able to travel. But the rehab has been going. We’re doing what we’re supposed to be doing to try to get back on the timeline we talked about getting back on.”Butler, who the Chicago Bulls selected with the 30th pick in the 2011 Draft and carved a niche in the league through hard work and mental toughness, said he has enjoyed watching different young players in the Warriors organization earn their opportunity as the team has been overwhelmed by injuries throughout the season.“There’s still some wonderful guys that are taking advantage of their opportunity with some guys being down,” Butler said. “That was me at one point in my Chicago days. So I get very happy, and it makes me smile when I see people play well. And then, I got my family around, my kids around, and then, I just know that I’m working back towards something. It all keeps it in perspective for me.”Butler’s name was mentioned in trade speculation near the deadline, but the Warriors clarified to him at the time that they weren’t planning to move him. He reiterated on Monday that he never felt like he was going to be part of a deal, even after his season-ending injury.“I wasn’t too worried about it,” he said.Butler said he has a “fancy chart” hanging on his wall as he works through the week-by-week rehab process, noting that the next step is getting rid of the crutches in about a week. He said he is looking at the chart all the time to stay motivated.“Everything we do in rehab is about competing,” Butler said. “Whether it’s today versus yesterday, what my numbers are compared to other people’s past — I (won’t say) any names. It’s competing to see whether you can be better than you were yesterday. So the whole thing makes me lock in because I at least get to compete that way.”Your browser does not support the video tag.How do the Warriors cope without Jimmy?Dave DuFourButler said he doesn’t have individual former players he’s competing against, but the chart is something he focuses on regarding day-to-day progress.“I’m just gonna focus in on me,” Butler said. “And come back the best version of myself.”In 14 seasons, Butler said he has never seen a team get derailed by injuries quite like this. Warriors star Stephen Curry has missed a month and a half because of a lingering runner’s knee issue. His return to the floor remains unclear, even though he hopes to return before the regular season ends. A variety of different Warriors have missed games because of injury — a pattern that Butler admits he hasn’t seen before.“Not like this,” Butler said. “Injuries happen, but with all the injuries, there are some bright spots. Guys have been taking (advantage of) the opportunity of guys being injured. That’s just the way that the league goes. Next man up mentality. You show up, and you show out. A lot of these young guys have been collectively putting in the effort to give us a chance to win. And that’s really all that you can ask for. They’re putting the world on notice on who they are, too.”Butler’s arrival brought an added emotional lift for the Warriors, who came into Monday’s game on a season-long five-game losing skid. Warriors coach Steve Kerr mentioned before the game that he has been texting with Butler since the injury, and the pair shared a couple of minutes at his locker before Monday’s game. It’s a long road back for Butler before he plays in an NBA game again, but it’s a challenge he’s wrapping his head around in real time, one day at a time.“I do want to come back,” Butler said. “I can’t say when. Obviously, as early as I can to help my guys win some games. But you’ll probably hear me say from time to time (in this process), whenever my body’s ready … whenever my body’s ready, I promise I’m trying to get back out there.”
